CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's fundamental health is strong: Q1 2026 showed +22.2% YoY revenue growth and +30.2% YoY EPS growth, with a $51B+ order backlog providing multi-year visibility. ROE is high at ~50%, margins are solid (gross 35%, operating 17.7%), and the company just raised its dividend 8% (32nd consecutive year of increases). The services business and AI data center power demand provide structural tailwinds. However, valuation is extremely stretched: P/E has expanded from ~17x a year ago to ~44x currently, P/B from 9.5x to 22.4x, and the stock is up ~112% over the past year. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.6B in 2026 are compressing margins (operating margin fell 270bps in Q4 2025), and net income actually declined 17.8% in FY2025 despite revenue growth. The QoQ revenue trajectory was slightly negative (-1.3%) and operating cash flow dropped 50% QoQ. At 44x earnings for a cyclical industrial, the market is pricing in near-perfect execution on AI/data center growth while tariff and macro risks (China weakness, rising rates, geopolitical tensions) remain material. The dividend increase and strong backlog provide modest near-term support, but the valuation leaves little margin of safety.
